overview.text: The Great Plains Rat Snake is a harmless rat snake of the central United States and northern Mexico. It often lives on farms, where it hunts rats and mice.

identification.text: Light grey or tan with dark grey, brown or greenish-grey blotches down the back. Stripes on each side of the head meet in a point between the eyes.

distribution.label: Native
distribution.text: The central USA - south-western Illinois, Missouri and Kansas west to south-eastern Colorado and eastern New Mexico and south through Texas, with isolated areas in Utah - and northern Mexico.

habitat.text: Open grassland and light woodland, coastal plains, semi-dry areas and rocky hills; often on farmland where rodents are plentiful.

diet.text: Mainly rodents; also birds and sometimes snakes, lizards and frogs.

funfacts.text: Because it turns up on farms it is sometimes wrongly called a 'chicken snake'.

recognise.text: Grey or tan with darker blotches.
Head stripes that meet in a point between the eyes.
